data.narrative:
Cortical Labs is a Series A-stage AI & Software company founded by Hon Weng Chong and Andy Kitchen that has raised $11M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private firms operating in the same sector and stage window, including Scale AI, Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, and Black Forest Labs.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $11M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yielding a $22M implied valuation. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $15.3B (range: $3.2B to $29.0B). The wide dispersion reflects material stage and valuation heterogeneity within frontier AI, with Reflection AI at $25.0B and Scale AI at $29.0B on the high end versus Black Forest Labs at $3.2B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range with a low of $19M, median of $7.7B, and high of $17.6B. The disparity between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects the outsized valuations commanded by leading AI software companies at comparable or adjacent stages. Key uncertainties center on whether Cortical Labs' technology and market position merit valuation toward the peer median or represent earlier-stage risk warranting a discount. Additional clarity on proprietary assets, revenue traction, and competitive differentiation would be necessary to narrow this range materially.
